Few professions shape daily life as visibly as civil engineering, and that is what first drew me toward it. Growing up fascinated by how bridges, roads, and skylines shape the way people live, travel, and connect, I was drawn to civil engineering because it offered the chance to turn problem-solving and creativity into infrastructure that serves entire communities. Over time, that interest became a clear professional direction: I want to contribute as a Civil Engineer by helping architects, contractors, and stakeholders work smarter through designs that balance safety, efficiency, and cost. I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and through that academic foundation I completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes, experiences that strengthened my interest in turning technical requirements into practical, buildable solutions that balance safety, cost, and long-term performance.

My academic and project experience has also shown me how I work in practice. In one role, I needed to use a new technique that the work required; within a couple of months I had learned it well enough to apply it independently in my own tasks. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on, and I value those moments because they reflect the importance of clear communication and steady coordination. Just as importantly, I complete the work assigned to me within the agreed scope and schedule, which has helped projects move forward steadily.

One of my favourite memories was taking my family to a bridge project I had helped deliver, where my nephew became captivated by a tunnel I had helped build and began explaining it to strangers as though he had built it himself. That moment captured exactly why this profession matters to me. I am now eager to bring my background, practical judgement, and commitment to well-coordinated, lasting infrastructure into a Civil Engineer role where I can continue learning, contribute, and help create projects that people can rely on.

Few things are more satisfying than taking raw materials and shaping them into something lasting, useful, and beautifully made. That is what drew me to carpentry: the chance to combine creativity with practical problem-solving and to build spaces and furniture that people rely on every day. One of my favourite memories was bringing my family to see a community project I had helped build, only for my youngest relative to run straight to a bench I had made and proudly call it “our family bench.” It stayed with me because it showed me that carpentry does not only create structures; it creates stories people carry with them. Originally from Bangladesh, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and across my work I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes.

My academic background gave me a strong foundation for careful planning, precise execution, and seeing a space through properly, while my professional experience has shown me how much I enjoy working in a space where design choices and practical finishing meet. In one role, I moved into an unfamiliar area of work and, within about a quarter, was handling it independently, which taught me how to absorb new processes quickly and apply them in day-to-day tasks. On another project, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time at the same stage of the process, so I introduced a simple adjustment to the process that reduced delays and saved time across the job. I also make a point of sharing information about my own work when teammates need it, whether that means clarifying measurements, passing on updates, or helping someone follow the next step.

What continues to excite me about carpentry is the connection between design and finish. I am especially drawn to work that combines cutting, fitting, and finishing, because it requires precision on every level from the smallest details to the final finish. I am now looking to bring that approach to a Carpenter role where I can keep learning, contribute dependable work, and build spaces and furniture that people use every day.

Order has always felt most meaningful to me when it helps people and products stay connected, which is why logistics became the natural direction for me. I am originally from the Netherlands, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. What first drew me in was the way planning, timing, and communication can turn uncertainty into something reliable and practical. That connection became even more personal during a family road trip when we unexpectedly passed one of the regional warehouses I help support, and my family insisted we stop so I could show them “where all the planning happens.” Seeing them connect my behind-the-scenes work to the products arriving in stores made the profession feel immediate and real.

Through doctoral study and subsequent project work, I have built a structured approach to coordinating people, timelines, and processes, and I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes that strengthened my interest in work where planning leads to visible results. In one project, I had to use a method that was completely new to me; within a few weeks I was applying it confidently, and soon after I was the person colleagues came to when they needed someone to walk them through it. On another occasion, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time at the same handover point, so I introduced a simple adjustment to the process that reduced delays and saved time across the group.

In addition, colleagues and supervisors regularly came to me with difficult questions, including issues outside my immediate area, and I became used to helping them work through them step by step. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when the project demanded it so that it could be completed properly. Although my interest began with a simple wish to make life easier for others, it has grown into a clear professional direction. Consequently, I am eager to bring this combination of structured thinking, practical coordination, and steady follow-through to a Logistics Coordinator role.
